one-check-per-line.why: all 4 lines quoted in order, checks numbered 1 to 4

no-restated-rules.why: no branch, base, branch-name rule or return mechanics named

builder-criteria.why: all 4 lines quoted in the builder brief

words-only.why: Checks 1, 2 and 4 stay within their expect lines. Check 1's cases are plain left-padding, Check 2's inputs are all already width or longer, and Check 4 is just exit code 0 with fail 0. Check 3 breaks the criterion. Its FAIL condition uses a regex, `"^#{1,6}\\s+`?" + k + "\\b"`, that only matches a markdown heading starting with the function's name. The expect line says only "a section for every function", so a section headed "## The padLeft helper" or "## Function: padLeft" would meet the words but fail the check. That exact heading-form rule is stricter than the words and should be under Advisory, not in PASS/FAIL. PASS also requires "its own heading with a description beneath it" and FAIL on "no describing content". That is arguably part of what a section is, but it is still a judgment the words don't strictly force. So the criterion does not hold for the whole output.

runs-as-written.why: I checked every command in both briefs: `npm test`, the two padLeft behaviour checks run with `node --input-type=module -e`, and the README-section script that appears in both briefs. index.js, README.md and test/strutil.test.js exist at this commit, and `npm test` maps to "node --test". padLeft is added by an earlier builder step. Each -e program is in single quotes and contains only double quotes and backticks, so "\\s" and "\\b" reach JavaScript as the regex escapes \s and \b. The JavaScript is valid: ES module imports, a default import of node:fs, Object.keys on the module namespace, and destructuring for...of loops. Calls such as padLeft("hello", 3) pass undefined, so the default fill applies. I saw only the scripts field of package.json, so "type": "module" is unconfirmed, but current Node detects ES module syntax anyway. No command breaks.

catches-traps.why: All three must_catch items are handled. (1) Builder step 2: "Also add the missing `## slugify(s)` section", next to the padLeft section; Context notes README has "NO section for slugify". (2) Verifier check 3 runs a script that reads the module's exports at the PR head, prints "exports: …" and reports "MISSING" for any export without a README heading. PASS needs every exported function to have a described section, "including slugify… and padLeft". FAIL triggers on MISSING for any name. (3) Verifier check 1 calls padLeft("42", 5) with no fill and expects "   42", so space padding is checked.

avoids-must-not.why: I checked both must_not items against the verifier's checks and the builder brief. Item 1 holds: Check 3 runs every exported function through a heading regex and must print ALL PRESENT. The PASS text names slugify, "which had no section before this change", so a README with only a padLeft section would print MISSING: slugify and fail. Item 2 holds: Checks 1 and 2 only test left padding, the default space fill, exact width and returning s unchanged, using fill values of one character or none. Multi-character fill is "advisory… do not fail on it", and nothing counts parameters. Check 3's regex takes any heading level from # to ######, with or without a backtick, and does not require the `## name(args)` form. That form appears only as builder guidance, not as a PASS/FAIL condition. Asking for content under each heading is a fair reading of "a section". Check 4 needs only exit code 0 and fail 0.

methods-private.why: The criterion is not met because the builder brief carries the verifier's probes. Builder step 5 copies verifier Check 3's inline script character for character: `node --input-type=module -e 'import * as m from "./index.js"; ... console.log(miss.length ? "MISSING: " ... : "ALL PRESENT");'`. It also gives the same pass condition: it "must print ALL PRESENT". No expect line or issue proof names this command; expect line 4 names only `npm test`, so the exception does not cover it. The builder's examples also repeat verifier test cases with their expected outputs: padLeft('42', 5, '0') === '00042' and padLeft('42', 5) === '   42' are in Check 1, and padLeft('123456', 5, '0') === '123456' is in Check 2. Telling the builder to run `npm test` and write its own tests is allowed. But the shared script and the shared input/output pairs break the rule.
